quarterly_data.signal: CEO: 'an important improvement in market conditions' since the last report, driven primarily by strong growth in AI demand and, to a lesser extent, additions to mobile and automotive capacity; renewed growth for high-end mobile and automotive in Q1. Strategy: supporting customer adoption of the wafer-level assembly and 2.5D AI portfolio and ramping the supply chain and production personnel to meet increased order levels; increasing service and support in Taiwan and Korea in anticipation of increased hybrid bonding activities there. New products and use cases announced this year for logic, memory, co-packaged optics and consumer applications suggest the pace of hybrid bonding adoption is increasing ahead of many new AI-related products anticipated in the 2027 till 2030 period. As customers' production lines load, BESI sees 'a broad increase in the demand of service spares and retrofit kits'.

CEO on Q2 2026 order intake: 'continued momentum, a continuing trend' - 'we're in an upcycle', and as long as there are no signs of saturation in the end markets it can be expected to continue; 'So far this quarter, we have seen no change.' BESI has ramped its capacities 50% quarter-over-quarter in past upcycles and is ramping again now - 'That's as much as we can.'

CEO on hybrid bonder configurations: the overwhelming majority of tools are still standalone in this initial phase - the Taiwanese customer uses standalone for flexibility (multiple customers, die sizes and process requirements) but that is 'very likely in the future to change to an automated line concept simply because of process requirements' (hybrid bonding needs zero particles, best met in an automated line such as Applied Materials' Kinex).

connects_to.relationship: EMIB module-placement systems (customer named by the filer)

contracts.signal: CEO Richard Blickman: BESI has been involved 'since the very beginning in placement of these EMIB modules'; Intel has 'a significant capacity installed, which we delivered the systems placing those modules'. On rising EMIB demand: 'That could be a positive business impact, but as things with Intel develop as they do, we first need to see more evidence.'

players.product: hybrid bonding and thermo-compression bonders for die stacking

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on hybrid bonding versus TCB in HBM: for a given volume 'it will be less TC if one uses hybrids. That's an offset in the same end volume' - more confirmation 'from the Samsung side' expected by the middle or the end of this year. HBM versus logic: far less I/O and a less critical bond pad pitch, but vertical stacks of thinner dies, so a different process; devices may end up in quality classes. Why memory makers are 'putting far more effort into the adoption of hybrid bonding': 'the proven performance upgrades are driving that adoption by an end customer, and that's a very big customer.'
